candidate.educational_objective: Recommend 400 mcg folic acid daily before conception and during early pregnancy for an average-risk person who may become pregnant.

options.A: Begin folic acid only after pregnancy is confirmed by a missed period, because neural tube development does not begin until later in the first trimester.
options.B: Wait until the second trimester to begin supplementation, because folic acid has no preventive role during the weeks around conception.
options.C: Rely on naturally occurring food folate alone before pregnancy, then begin a supplement only if prenatal testing identifies a fetal abnormality.
options.D: Take 400 mcg of folic acid daily before conception and during early pregnancy, because neural tube formation and closure occur very early.

candidate.rationale: For an average-risk person who could become pregnant, CDC recommends 400 mcg of folic acid daily. Neural tube formation and closure occur very early in pregnancy, often before pregnancy is recognized, so supplementation should begin before conception and continue during early pregnancy rather than waiting for a positive test or a later trimester.
candidate.source_claim_supported: An average-risk person who can become pregnant should take 400 mcg folic acid daily before conception and during early pregnancy because neural-tube development occurs very early.
candidate.source_document_title: CDC — Folic Acid: Sources and Recommended Intake / Neural Tube Defects

candidate.stem: A client who may become pregnant within the next several months asks when to begin folic acid to reduce the risk of neural tube defects. Which recommendation is most appropriate for an average-risk client?
